issues.display_title: Issue #1257: Editor: the Size slider can widen a door or window past the end of its wall
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #1241 (noted in PR #1254). The door/window Size slider now reaches 10 m, but it has never limited an opening to its wall. setSelectedOpeningWidth (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts) widens the opening around its centre, whatever the wall's length. So a 10 m width runs past the end of a shorter wall, and an opening near a wall's end overruns it even when it is narrower than the wall. The 3 m slider could already do this on short walls. The #1241 demo shows a 6 m shopfront door widened past the end of its diagonal wall on Square One Mall V6.

What exists already

Dragging an opening's own handle already keeps it on its wall. src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/editing.ts has:

  • wallForOpening — finds the wall an opening sits on;
  • openingParamOnWall — its centre's position along the wall, its length and its direction;
  • placeOpeningOnWall — puts it back at most the wall's length long, sliding it along the wall so both ends stay on it.

Scope

  1. The Size slider keeps an opening on its wall. For each selected opening that sits on a wall:

    • its width is at most the wall's length;
    • near an end, it slides along the wall instead of running past the end.

    Reuse wallForOpening, openingParamOnWall and placeOpeningOnWall.

  2. An opening on no wall resizes around its centre, as today.

  3. The readout shows the real width. Today the toolbar shows the slider's own value (openingWidth in FloorplanEditor is set from the slider). Once the width can be limited, it must read the engine back (getOpeningWidth) after each change.

Not in this task: stopping at a neighbouring opening on the same wall.

Acceptance criteria

  • On a 7 m wall, sliding a door to 10 m makes it 7 m, and the readout says 7.00 m.
  • A door near a wall's end, widened, stays entirely on its wall.
  • An opening that sits on no wall resizes as before.
  • Unit tests cover all three.

RESULT

video-1257-opening-wall-clamp.mp4

Released to main in 965ccf9e (PR #1258 → development de1e4e1e, release PR #1259). The Deploy succeeded.

Fix (commit bee9830a):

  • setSelectedOpeningWidth (editor/model-sync.ts):
    • an opening on a wall is placed with wallForOpening, openingParamOnWall and placeOpeningOnWall, the same placement its drag handle uses;
    • it is at most the wall's length, and slides along the wall instead of running past an end;
    • the direction it was drawn in is kept;
    • an opening on no wall still grows around its centre.
  • SelectionToolbars reads the width back with getOpeningWidth() after each change, so the readout shows the opening's real width.

Tests: 4 new tests in opening-width.test.ts, and the new SelectionToolbars.openingWidth.test.tsx. All 3 mutants are caught. pnpm test (3076), lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked, real Chrome on a scratch copy of Square One Mall V6 per run, all deleted (.playwright-mcp/demo/1257/check-clamp.mjs). On Level 1, the slider is pressed to its end:

Door development (before) fix production
42: 6 m, near the end of its 10.24 m wall 10 m, past the end (t 0.22 / 1.20) 10 m, slid onto the wall (t 0.02 / 1.00) 10 m, t 0.02 / 1.00
32: 4.31 m on a 7.16 m wall 10 m, past the ends 7.16 m, readout 7.16 m 7.16 m, readout 7.16 m

Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1257/video-1257-opening-wall-clamp.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1262: Editor: Add Floor breaks onto two lines beside a long building name
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From #1260. In the editor's sidebar, the + Add Floor button breaks onto two lines ("+ Add / Floor") when the label beside it is long, as on Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo ("FLOOR in Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo").

Cause

src/components/editor/EditorPanel.tsx, the Floor header:

  • The "in {building}" text already truncates, but the span around the label has no min-w-0, so it never shrinks below its content.
  • The button has neither shrink-0 nor whitespace-nowrap, so it is the button that gets squeezed, and its text wraps.

Scope

  1. The label shrinks and the building name ends in "…".
  2. Add Floor stays on one line at its full width.

Acceptance criteria

  • With a long building name, + Add Floor stays on one line and the building name is cut with "…".
  • A short name shows in full, as today.
  • Unit test.

RESULT

video-1262-add-floor-nowrap.mp4

Released to main in c97962ee (PR #1264 → development dc66918c, release PR #1266 together with #1263). The Deploy succeeded.

Fix (commit 809782c9): in EditorPanel.tsx, the Floor header's label span gets min-w-0 (and "FLOOR" shrink-0), so the building name ends in "…". The Add Floor button gets shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap, and the header gets a gap-2.

Tests: the new EditorPanel.addFloor.test.tsx. pnpm test, lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked, real Chrome on a scratch copy of Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo per run, deleted (.playwright-mcp/demo/1262/check-add-floor.mjs):

Add Floor Building name
development (before) 2 lines in full
fix 1 line cut with "…"
production 1 line cut with "…"

Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1262/video-1262-add-floor-nowrap.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1263: Viewer Overview: a multi-storey building is drawn as its lowest floor raised to full height, and place markers still show
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From #1261 (Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, 34 levels). In the viewer's Overview, the building is one huge block, much wider and taller than the real tower: Mappedin shows a podium with a slender tower on it. Overview also shows place markers (Retail/Office, Parking Garage, Loading Dock…). The report asks that Overview show only building names, with no tooltips or information markers.

Cause

  • The block. outdoorGeoJson (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) builds the Overview block from the areas of the building's lowest floor only, raised to the building's total height. On this project:
    • the podium floors are about 139 × 108 m, and the tower floors about 25 × 64 m;
    • there are 36 floors;
    • so the Overview is a 139 × 108 m box about 108 m tall.
  • The markers. MapObjectMarkers stays mounted in Overview with siteScaleOnly (#963). It keeps every object big enough on screen, the "plots a visitor lands on", which is why the large retail and parking areas get markers there.

Scope

  1. Overview stacks every floor at its own height.
    • Each floor's areas stand from that floor's base, the sum of the heights of the floors below it, to its top.
    • So the podium and the tower take their real shapes.
    • Each part wears its own area's colour, by the #1249 rule, and nested areas are cut out of the area around them.
    • Standalone Areas stay low pads, on the lowest floor only.
    • A floor with walls but no areas is a block of its bounding box, as today.
  2. Overview shows only building names. No object markers and no tooltips. The building label (icon and name) stays.
  3. Inside a building nothing changes. Other buildings drawn as shells use the same stacked shape.

#1247 Q3 ("colours come from the ground floor") no longer applies: with floors stacked, the roofs you see are the top floor of each part.

Acceptance criteria

  • On Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, Overview shows a wide podium and a narrow tower on it, matching the floors' outlines, not one box.
  • Overview shows the building's name and no place markers.
  • Square One Mall V6's Overview still shows its rooms' colours (#1249).
  • Unit tests: stacked heights and footprints, the lowest-floor pads, and the no-area fallback.

RESULT

video-1263-overview-stacked-floors.mp4

Released to main in c97962ee (PR #1265 → development bfc63af2, release PR #1266 together with #1262). The Deploy succeeded.

Fix (commit 70eb610f):

  • outdoorGeoJson stacks every floor, from levelBaseHeights to base + that floor's height × z-scale:
    • parts keep their area's colour (#1249) and nested areas are cut out;
    • standalone Areas are pads on the lowest floor only;
    • a floor with walls but no areas is a slate bounding box at its own height;
    • the building label stays on the lowest floor.
  • PreviewOverlay mounts no MapObjectMarkers in Overview. Zoomed out on a project that stays indoors (#976), the site-scale markers stay.

Tests: the #549/#884 and buildingHeights tests are updated for stacked parts, with 5 new stacking tests and the new PreviewOverlay.overviewMarkers.test.tsx (3). All mutants are caught. pnpm test, lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked, real Chrome (.playwright-mcp/demo/1263/check-overview.mjs; screenshots in the same folder):

Hi-rise Overview Markers (hi-rise / Square One)
development (before) one 139 × 108 m box 15 / 22
fix a stepped podium with the tower on it 0 / 0
production the tower on its podium, building name only 0 / 0

Square One's Overview keeps its rooms' colours.

Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1263/video-1263-overview-stacked-floors.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1267: Preview: hover highlight flickers between rooms that are not under the cursor
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported with a screen recording (Square One Mall V6, preview, Level 2). With the cursor resting inside Rolex Boutique, the hover highlight flickers between Holt Renfrew, the large closed room far to the left, and Aesop, the shop below. Rolex Boutique itself never lights. Sampled at 60 fps, Holt Renfrew is highlighted in most frames and Aesop in a few.

Cause

  • The preview's hover and click handlers (src/components/editor/preview/usePreviewSelectionLayers.ts) take e.features[0] from the area extrusion layers.
  • Inside Rolex Boutique, MapLibre's queryRenderedFeatures returns two areas with exactly the same base and top (3 / 4.6):
    • Rolex Boutique, whose footprint contains the cursor's ground point;
    • Holt Renfrew, whose footprint does not.
  • Near the Rolex/Aesop wall, Aesop is returned too.
  • With equal heights, the order of e.features changes as the cursor drifts a pixel, so the highlight jumps between them: 8 flips in 47 samples in a probe. A click there can open the wrong card too.
  • The data is fine: Rolex and Aesop do not overlap Holt Renfrew.
  • The editor's Map tab (Editor3DMapView.tsx) takes e.features[0] the same way, and registers its handler once per layer, so one mouse move can fire several events that overwrite each other.

Scope

  1. A helper picks, from the queried area features, the first one whose footprint (outer ring minus holes) contains the cursor's ground point (e.lngLat). If none does (a tall roof seen at a pitch), it falls back to e.features[0].
  2. Use it for the preview's area hover and area click.
  3. Use it for the editor Map tab's area hover, registered once over all area layers.

Acceptance criteria

  • On Square One Mall V6, Level 2, a cursor resting inside Rolex Boutique highlights Rolex Boutique only, steadily.
  • Clicking there opens Rolex Boutique's card.
  • Unit tests: the helper picks the containing feature, respects holes, and falls back when none contains.

RESULT

video-1267-hover-pick.mp4

Released to main in 3969592d (PR #1268 → development dfa63c8f, release PR #1269). The Deploy succeeded.

Fix (commit 0da13405, new src/lib/map/pickAreaFeature.ts):

  • cursorAtAltitude(map, point) gives the cursor's ray, from the camera (map.transform.getCameraLngLat() / getCameraAltitude()) through the ground point, crossing a given altitude.
  • pickAreaFeature(features, pointAt) returns the first feature, in depth order, whose footprint (outer minus holes) holds that ray at the feature's own roof height. Otherwise it falls back to features[0].
  • Used by the preview's area hover and click, and the editor Map tab's hover, which is now registered once over all area layers.

The scope said "the cursor's ground point". At a pitch, that is not what is seen: a 4.6 m roof sits about 5 m toward the camera at zoom 20.5 and a 49° pitch. The fix therefore tests at roof height.

Tests: 11 new tests across pickAreaFeature, cursorAtAltitude and usePreviewSelectionLayers.pick. All mutants are caught. pnpm test (3096), lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked, real Chrome on the public /v/UkZnTKwv (.playwright-mcp/demo/1267/check-hover.mjs). The cursor sweeps the shops around Rolex Boutique at zooms 19.8, 20.5 and 21.2, compared against the roof seen, computed independently in the page:

Lit room = roof under the cursor
development (before) 34 of 232 wrong: Holt Renfrew lit over Rolex Boutique, Aesop, Alo Yoga…
fix 0 of 228 wrong
production 0 of 228 wrong; a click in Rolex Boutique opens its card

Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1267/video-1267-hover-pick.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1271: Viewer: let the owner choose which toolbar buttons are shown (Search Area, Direction, Event)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From albug's feedback ("I should be able to select what buttons I see here", screenshot of the viewer's top-left toolbar). The decisions are in #1270.

Today

The viewer's toolbar (src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx) always shows Search Area, Direction and Event, plus the building and floor pickers. The owner can't turn any of them off; they are only hidden automatically in Overview and on panorama-only projects (#1214).

Scope

  1. A project setting saved in the project's map data (canvasData), like "Show connection lines on live" (#544) and the room-outline setting (#1020). No backend or API change. A project without the setting shows every button, as today.
  2. Edit Project Info gets a checkbox each for Search Area, Direction and Event, next to "Show connection lines on live". All are checked by default.
  3. An unchecked button is hidden from the toolbar on every surface: the owner's Preview, the published link, Embed Map and Embed to Virtual Tour.
  4. Only the toolbar button is hidden. The information card's Directions button and its events still open Direction and Event (#1270 Q3 b).
  5. The building and floor pickers can't be turned off (#1270 Q1, Q4). Overview and panorama-only projects keep hiding buttons as they do now.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unchecking Search Area, Direction or Event in Edit Project Info and saving hides that button in Preview and on the published link; checking it again brings it back.
  • The setting survives a reload of the editor and of the published link.
  • Existing projects (no setting saved) show all three buttons.
  • With Direction hidden, the information card's Directions button still opens Direction.
  • Unit tests.

RESULT

video-1271-viewer-toolbar-buttons.mp4

Released to main in de269d96 (PR #1272 → development b6269924, release PR #1273). Deploy succeeded.

What changed

  • Setting: canvasData.viewerButtons?: { search?, direction?, event? }, where false hides that button. It is saved with the project's map data like showPanoConnections (#544) and roomOutlines (#1020), so no backend or API change. A project without it shows all three.
  • Edit Project Info: a "Viewer toolbar buttons" group with a checkbox each for Search Area, Direction and Event, under "Show connection lines on live". It writes the setting only when the choice changed.
  • Toolbar: PreviewControls hides a button set to false in Preview, on the published link and in both embeds. Overview and panorama-only projects still hide buttons as before.
  • Per #1270: only the toolbar button is hidden, so the information card still opens Direction and Event. The building and floor pickers have no checkbox.

Files: src/store/useMapStore.types.ts, src/components/editor/EditFileModal.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx.

Tests

  • PreviewControls.test.tsx (+1), EditFileModal.viewerButtons.test.tsx (5) and PreviewOverlay.viewerButtons.test.tsx (3). The overlay test includes the card's Direction button opening Direction while Direction is hidden.
  • 7 of 7 mutants were caught. pnpm test (3105), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked on production (map-thru.com) with a published scratch copy of Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, deleted afterwards (.playwright-mcp/demo/1271/check-buttons.mjs, 7/7):

  • With no setting, Preview shows all three buttons.
  • After Direction and Event are unchecked and saved, the server copy has viewerButtons = {"direction":false,"event":false,"search":true}.
  • The choice survives an editor reload.
  • Preview and /v/{key} show only Search Area, and the floor picker is still there.
  • Checking Direction again brings it back on /v/{key}.

Demo video (A/B): .playwright-mcp/demo/1271/video-1271-viewer-toolbar-buttons.mp4.

Commit: f2ed39f3
